passages.note: The enrolled text prints the operative strict-scrutiny exemption standard the vote was taken on, but it names no voter and a No vote on it cannot fix which rung the voter holds.
The bill-details page confirms the instrument and its enactment as Public Law 3 and shows Clere is not among the authors, co-authors or sponsors, so it adds no act of his beyond the roll call.

rows.reasoning: The only act in the sources is Clere's Nay on SB 101 (2015), the single-subject Religious Freedom Restoration bill whose operative section says "a governmental entity may not substantially burden a person's exercise of religion" absent a compelling interest and least restrictive means. Voting against that bill rules out the rungs that "allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs" and that grant "complete autonomy in their operations and hiring practices", but it does not separate "prohibit religious exemptions from civil rights and anti-discrimination laws" from "protect religious freedom while ensuring it doesn't override anti-discrimination protections in employment and housing" or from "balance protecting religious practices with maintaining equal treatment under the law for all citizens". Ruling out the other rungs is not evidence for the one left, so the row is direction-only.
